name: Lagoons of New Caledonia: Reef Diversity and Associated Ecosystems
blurb: Seagrass, dugongs and sharks inside one of the largest reef lagoons.

tip.title: Remove the green turtles
tip.text: Adult turtles graze seagrass and are prey for tiger sharks. Set Green sea turtle to -100% and watch the seagrass and the tiger shark respond.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage: Lagoons of New Caledonia

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.desc: Tropical sun powers the seagrass, algae and phytoplankton of the shallow lagoon, and the algae living inside reef corals.
Rivers carry soil into the lagoon. Mangroves trap some of it, but heavy runoff from mining and grazing has buried reefs in silt.

nodes.name: Bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down dead seagrass, mangrove leaves and animals, returning nutrients to the sediment.
Low seagrass meadows in the shallow lagoon, the main food of dugongs and adult green turtles.
Mangrove forests fringe the shore and help retain sediment before it reaches the reef.
Algae growing on reef rock and sand, grazed by parrotfish and surgeonfish.
Drifting microscopic algae that feed zooplankton and corals. General ecological knowledge.
Adults graze mostly seagrass, nibbling blade tops so beds stay healthy. The lagoon is an important nesting site.
Feeds mainly on seagrass. New Caledonia holds the third largest dugong population in the world, and hunting is banned there.
Most species scrape algae from reef rock with their beaks, which keeps algae from overgrowing the reef.
Reef fish that graze algae. General ecological knowledge for the family.

nodes.name: Copepods
nodes.desc: Tiny drifting crustaceans that graze phytoplankton and feed many reef animals.
Branching and table corals build the reef structure. The lagoon coral diversity matches or exceeds the Great Barrier Reef.

nodes.name: Common coral trout
nodes.desc: An ambush predator of the reef that eats mainly fish, including parrotfish. Caught here by line and spear.
Eats living hard coral, especially Acropora, leaving white skeleton. Outbreaks can devastate reefs.
Wide-ranging predator that eats turtles, dugongs, fish and sea snakes, and also scavenges carcasses.
